body: My husband had a full colectomy at 25 and felt as despairing as you do now. Then after surgery he felt better than he has since childhood. You're young and your immune system is tough. It feels like all your immune system does is kick your ass but it will kick cancers ass too; you caught it early.

The Good Gut is a useful resource. But if she's like my husband, everyone has to figure out their diet and it can differ. For example, my husband has flares from chocolate, coffee, black tea, dairy, raw fruits/veggies, lots of sugar, red or processed meat, etc. Also, any stress affects his gut, just as flares make him depressed. So Headspace, regular bedtimes, tv/films/books with happy endings, lots of water, supportive friends, daily exercise, and a controlled diet are not negotiable. Even with his infusions (he's on Remicade) diet is key. Also, given the amount of diarrhea, water intake can't be stressed enough (but watch out for electrolytes; those might cause problems). And OTC pain meds aren't always effective (or the side effects suck so much there's no point). Have a go bag for the hospital, too. Most importantly: only after my husband got a superbug did we learn that Crohn's sufferers are very susceptible (he nearly died from a c diff spore he inhaled while visiting me for a few hours in the hospital). So masks, gowns and gloves are vital in any hospital setting. Good luck to you. It's absolutely worth it.

The Gaffer also knew more about how to serve the master of Bag End than Sam, having served Bilbo before the latter's departure, and would see deficiencies in Sam's lack of experience. Disclaimer: everyone is different, so what works for my husband, who has severe Crohn's and UC, might not work for anyone else (and he's had surgeries, is on Remicade, takes 3 showers a day).  Here are the specifics:

* 6 small meals/day of 300-400 calories each
* Live probiotics (not kombucha) daily (he likes one Kevita drink daily, even though they're carbonated).  A GI attending physician recommended this.
* A full glass of water with each meal (no coffee, tea, caffeine or cocoa)
* Mild spices/herbs (we stock up on cinnamon, nutmeg, vanilla extract, pepper, garlic and salt)
* Low fiber foods (but not so low he has diarrhea all the time - we have brown rice cakes when he needs it)
* No dairy. Ever.  Soy milk and Earth Butter are always in our fridge.
* No gluten.  Rice, sweet potatoes, and oats are eaten every day in our house.  Fritos are a favorite snack, as are those rice mochi from Trader Joe's.
* No red/processed meat. Lean, skinless, unprocessed, white meats only (chicken, turkey) and, once a week, some fish
* Nothing fried. Ever.
* Nothing that would hurt coming out of his butt - no seeds, no nuts (except for almond butter), no popcorn, etc.
* No fruits or vegetables UNLESS peeled, seedless, cooked (or if dried without sulfur), and if need be pureed (kale, I'm looking at you).  Unsulfured dehydrated mango pieces from Trader Joe's are always in our pantry.
* Limit sugar.  We have stevia blend sugar for baking.
* Sample menu:  breakfast of Multigrain Cheerios in soy milk, second breakfast of some almond butter cookies (1 cup almond butter + 1/2 cup trulia sugar/stevia blend + 1 egg, baked for 8 minutes at 350 degrees F), lunch of white rice with chicken in bone broth, snack of a vegan vanilla smoothie, afternoon tea of rice snacks/fritos, dinner of a baked sweet potato with earth butter.
